stories.headline: US President Trump hints at new strikes on Iran as military tensions escalate
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump said on Friday that the United States may launch another attack on Iran. He called the potential military action another little Epic Fury. A joint Israeli-American military operation named Epic Fury launched at the end of February. That operation sparked the ongoing war with Iran.

A person briefed on war planning told NPR that both countries are preparing plans for an attack. They said the attack could happen after the US midterm elections. The US midterm elections are scheduled for November 3. Israel's election takes place on October 27. Almost 21 million Americans have already cast their ballots through mail-in or early voting.

Military assets are already moving into place in the region. Two US aircraft carrier strike groups are currently located in the Arabian Sea. A third carrier group is expected to arrive by late November.

Foreign ministers from eight European and Middle Eastern countries met at a summit in Istanbul. They urged the United States and Israel not to renew military attacks on Iran. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said that military intervention is not a solution. Fidan warned that new attacks would spread conflict across the entire region. Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia previously formed the Mecca defensive security pact in August.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi posted a warning on social media. Araghchi said any cooperation by regional states in an operation would face a decisive response.

Trump also spoke about Cuba at a South Florida rally on Friday. He said that US warships returning from Iran could stop near Cuba. He said this could happen before Secretary of State Marco Rubio negotiates a deal. The United States recently imposed further sanctions on the Cuban government. US officials expressed dissatisfaction with recent bilateral discussions. Cuba has been struggling with a severe economic and energy crisis since 2020.

Trump is also facing legal action at home. A federal magistrate judge ruled Donald Trump must sit for a deposition. The deposition is for his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC.

stories.headline: Israel orders West Bank lockdown after Hebron shooting kills two soldiers
stories.body:
The Israeli military launched a targeted operation near Hebron after a shooting killed two Israeli soldiers.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited Hebron and ordered a full lockdown of the occupied West Bank. Emergency responders reported five people were injured in the attack near Yehuda Junction. Some of the injured were in critical condition. The Israeli military reported that security forces killed two attackers involved in the shooting.

Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir said the attack shows a need to restrict Palestinian movement. Defence Minister Israel Katz said that clan neighbourhoods where attackers emerged from will be evacuated. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich posted a video of a bulldozer destroying a Palestinian home. The home was near the site of the firefight. But Israel's High Court issued a temporary order halting home demolitions in Hebron. The court ruled after an urgent petition was filed by a human rights lawyer.

More than 1,100 Palestinians have been killed in the West Bank since October 7, 2023. They were killed by Israeli forces or settlers.

stories.headline: Gunmen open fire inside Jordanian church funeral, killing seven people
stories.body:
Two masked gunmen opened fire at a church in Karak, Jordan, killing seven people. The shooting happened during a funeral procession inside a church in Hmoud.

At least 34 people were wounded in the attack. Witness Khalid al-Mdanat told BBC Arabic that the shooting inside the church lasted about 15 minutes. The gunmen then fled the scene in a pickup truck. Major General Obeidallah Maaytah reported that 27 wounded people remained hospitalized.

Jordanian Interior Minister Mazen Al-Faraya said that extremists carried out a horrific terrorist act. Prime Minister Jafar Hassan ordered a three-day period of national mourning starting Friday. King Abdullah II declared on social media that Jordan will confront the act with the harshest penalties.

Leaders across the region condemned the attack. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun called the shooting a heinous terrorist attack that violated religious values. Grand Imam of Al-Azhar Ahmed al-Tayeb also condemned the attack and offered condolences.

In 2016, a series of attacks by gunmen in Karak killed 10 people. Those victims included seven police officers.

stories.headline: French President Macron blames racism for drive-by shooting near Paris
stories.body:
French President Emmanuel Macron condemned a drive-by shooting near Paris as a premeditated racist attack.

The shooting spree happened across Trappes and La Verriere west of Paris. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said that a gunman opened fire across three separate locations over 15 minutes. One person died and at least five others were injured. A 12-year-old girl was among those wounded. Her mother told RTL her daughter was wearing a headscarf when she was shot eight times.

The mixed martial arts academy Atch Academy identified the dead young man as Pengo Bossio Wangi. La Verriere Mayor Nicolas Dainville said two wounded victims in his town were school cleaners of African origin. Trappes Mayor Ali Rabeh described the shooting as a racist attack probably motivated by Islamophobia.

French authorities identified the suspect as 39-year-old Kevin T. He had four previous convictions that were automatically expunged under French law. Police found a Sten-type submachine gun in his car. They also found three gas cylinders connected to a timer in his apartment. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu announced security forces are fully mobilized.

stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine announce brief local ceasefire in Oleshky
stories.body:
Russian and Ukrainian forces agreed to a localized ceasefire in the Ukrainian city of Oleshky.

The White House announced that First Lady Melania Trump helped broker the deal. US President Donald Trump said that her initiative led to the localized ceasefire. The ceasefire started at 02:00 GMT on October 27, 2026. The agreement aims to allow humanitarian aid entry and civilian evacuations.

Ukrainian MP Davyd Arakhamia confirmed that an operation to unblock Oleshky would begin after the announcement. Melania Trump arranged for news outlet Newsmax to document teams during the mission. Representatives of Melania Trump also helped return about 34 children between Russia and Ukraine since 2025.

Oleshky had a population of 24,000 before Russia's invasion in February 2022. About 90 percent of its territory flooded after the Kakhovka Dam collapsed in 2023. Ukrainian officials estimate about 6,000 people remain in Oleshky and surrounding areas. That number includes about 200 children.

stories.headline: Cybersecurity experts warn of global flaws in PHP web code
stories.body:
Cybersecurity firms discovered two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language.

Firm Wiz discovered the flaws alongside firm Calif in August. Wiz estimated the vulnerabilities affected about 70 percent of all websites worldwide. An unauthorized leak on Hacker News forced PHP developers to release emergency patches on October 21. PHP issued a security advisory on October 23 urging users to disable the session upload progress feature.

The US National Security Agency urged organizations to apply patches immediately. Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince reported that exploit attempts jumped from tens of thousands to millions. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi requested entities to apply patches or suspend websites.

Cybersecurity firm Censys detected about 36.7 million internet-facing services running vulnerable versions on October 22. Qualys identified 167 million PHP package installations across 12,000 organizations. About 73 percent were deployed on internet-facing assets. Multiple European government websites and the Port of Rotterdam temporarily took services offline.

stories.headline: Protests erupt across India over election panel voter roll review
stories.body:
Student groups organized a protest outside Mumbai University to demand changes to India's voter lists.

The Disha Students' Organisation and Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra held the demonstration on October 23, 2026. It took place outside the Kalina campus. Protesters demanded the complete withdrawal of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. They also called for the arrest of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Demonstrators asked for fresh elections using previous voter lists.

In addition, protesters called for the repeal of a 2023 law. That law governs how Election Commissioners are appointed. Dr. Pooja coordinates the Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra. She alleged that the voter list revision could disenfranchise several groups. She said it threatens Muslims, Dalits, Adivasis, and working-class voters.

The revision exercise has faced legal scrutiny before. On May 27, 2026, the Supreme Court of India upheld the validity of the revision conducted in Bihar. But protests against Gyanesh Kumar have expanded across India since October 2. Demonstrations have taken place in Delhi and other cities over the handling of the voter rolls.

Student leaders have faced police action during these demonstrations. All India Students' Association President Neha Bora was detained on October 16, 2026. She was detained during a protest near Barakhamba Road while demanding Kumar's resignation. A special executive magistrate directed Bora to furnish a personal bond of Rs 10,000 with a surety to maintain peace. Bora challenged the notice in court. The Delhi High Court dismissed her petition.

Internal tensions have also emerged within the Election Commission. Election Commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi wrote separate letters to Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan on July 29. They objected to a revised work allocation order. Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg issued that order. Garg issued it while filling in for Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu while Yeturu was on leave.

The disputed work allocation order was never implemented after the commissioners objected. Sandhu is a former Uttarakhand chief secretary with an MBBS, a history degree, and a law degree. Joshi is a former Haryana chief secretary with a doctorate in international economics.

A Cabinet note on August 3 proposed asking Kumar for his opinion on the complaint. But the Cabinet Secretariat declined to intervene. It said the letters were sent individually rather than as a formal commission communication.

stories.headline: India attributes fresh border tensions to Chinese patrol changes
stories.body:
Indian border police reported ongoing face-offs between Indian and Chinese troops in Arunachal Pradesh.

Indo-Tibetan Border Police Director General Shatrujeet Kapur made the statement publicly. The ITBP posted video footage of Kapur's speech online on Thursday night before deleting it. Tensions and face-offs occurred near Taksing in Upper Subansiri district during July and August. In July, Chinese troops pitched tents about 6 to 7 kilometers inside India's perceived border near Maja.

Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal addressed the situation. Jaiswal said that peace is disturbed when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns. China claims a large portion of Arunachal Pradesh as South Tibet and calls it Zangnan. The ITBP guards the 3,488-kilometer Line of Actual Control. The Home Ministry allocated Rs 400 crore to modernize the ITBP, with 70 percent designated for drone warfare.

Diplomatic and political discussions continue. Military commanders held talks in Arunachal Pradesh on September 6 and 7. Chinese President Xi Jinping advocated for a dual-track approach during a meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera called for an all-party delegation to inspect the border. Khera said India's trade deficit with China has reached $113 billion.
